# Address /code-review findings on tests/

## Context
`/code-review tests/` ran against the M1 commits just made (rb_find, rb_insert
tests, rb_validate) and returned 6 confirmed findings. The user asked to fix
all of them. Two are a real coverage gap in the algorithm's test surface,
one needs new test infrastructure, and three are cleanup/robustness nits:

1. **No test ever drives `insert_fixup`'s LL-rotation or either zigzag
   (LR/RL) double-rotation branch** — every existing insert sequence only
   hits the "uncle red" recolor case or a straight RR rotation. A bug in
   `src/rbtree.c:106-133` would pass the whole suite silently.
2. **`rb_validate` is never tested against a genuinely invalid tree** — it's
   only ever run on trees `insert_fixup` already made correct, so a broken
   validator (e.g. always returning 0) would go undetected.
3. `collect_key` in `tests/test_rbtree.c` writes into `order_ctx_t.keys[64]`
   with no bounds check.
4. `assert(rb_insert(...) == 0)` performs the mutating call *inside* the
   assert, so the call vanishes under `-DNDEBUG`.
5. The `{"mango","kiwi","pear","fig","lime","apricot"}` fixture is
   copy-pasted across two tests.
6. All 11 test functions repeat the same `rb_create` + `assert(!=NULL)`
   boilerplate.

Findings 1 and 2 need different fixes. (1) is testable with the *existing*
public API — specific 3-key insertion orders force each rotation branch, and
`rb_validate` (already proven correct by the M1 work) is the black-box
oracle that would catch a broken rotation. (2) is not testable through the
public API at all: `rb_insert`'s fixup always leaves a correct tree, and
`rb_delete` isn't implemented yet (M2), so there is currently no way to
produce an invalid tree through `include/rbtree.h`'s frozen surface. Testing
`rb_validate`'s negative cases requires white-box access to the internal
`rb_node_t`/`rbtree_t` layout, which only exists in `src/rbtree.c`.

## Approach for finding 2 (white-box negative tests)
Add a new test translation unit, `tests/test_rbtree_whitebox.c`, that does
`#include "../src/rbtree.c"` instead of `#include "rbtree.h"` — a standard
C "unity build" pattern that pulls in `rb_node_t`, `rbtree_t`, `RB_RED`/
`RB_BLACK`, `node_color`, and `rb_malloc`/`rb_free` as ordinary file-scope
symbols in this one file, with zero changes to the frozen header. It gets
its own Makefile binary (mirroring how `$(BIN)`/`$(FUZZBIN)` are already
defined) — compiled standalone, *not* linked against `src/rbtree.c` again
(that would duplicate every symbol).

In this file, a small `make_node(key, color)` helper (mallocs + copies the
key, mirroring `rb_insert`'s own allocation) builds hand-crafted 1-3 node
trees that each isolate exactly one of the 5 `rb_validate` checks:
- root red → violates "root is black"
- black `c` → red `b` → red `a` (three-deep chain, all same side) →
  violates "no red node has a red child"
- black root with only a black left child (no right) → violates
  "equal black-height on every path" (2 blacks down one side, 1 down other)
- black root, both children black, keys placed out of BST order → violates
  "strictly increasing in-order"
- a valid single-node tree with `t->size` manually set to 2 → violates
  "size matches node count"

Each asserts `rb_validate(t) != 0`. A sixth test builds a valid 3-node tree
by hand (black root, two red children) and asserts `rb_validate(t) == 0`,
as a control confirming the hand-built-tree methodology itself isn't just
producing garbage that happens to fail for unrelated reasons.

I checked each hand-built tree by tracing `check_black_height`/
`check_strictly_increasing`/`count_subtree` (added in the `rb_validate`
commit) by hand to confirm it isolates the intended single invariant.

## Approach for finding 1 (rotation coverage)
Add to `tests/test_rbtree.c`, using only the public API (mirrors the
existing `test_insert_ascending_run_findable` pattern of asserting
`rb_validate(t) == 0` after every insert):
- `"c", "b", "a"` — forces a left-left single rotation (`rotate_right`)
- `"c", "a", "b"` — forces a left-right zigzag (rotate left then right)
- `"a", "c", "b"` — forces a right-left zigzag (rotate right then left)

(Traced by hand against `insert_fixup` in `src/rbtree.c:94-136` to confirm
each sequence reaches the intended branch.) Combined with the existing
ascending-run test (which already covers straight RR rotations) and the
existing "uncle red" cases, this exercises every branch of `insert_fixup`.

## Cleanup items (findings 3, 4, 5, 6) — `tests/test_rbtree.c` only
- Split every `assert(rb_insert(...) == 0)` into `int rc = rb_insert(...);
  assert(rc == 0);` so the call survives `-DNDEBUG`.
- Add `assert(oc->count < sizeof(oc->keys) / sizeof(oc->keys[0]));` in
  `collect_key` before the write.
- Hoist the shared `{"mango","kiwi","pear","fig","lime","apricot"}` array
  (currently duplicated in `test_insert_multiple_findable` and
  `test_insert_foreach_sorted_order`) to one file-scope `static const
  char *const` array both tests read from.
- Add a `create_test_tree(value_free)` helper wrapping `rb_create` +
  `assert(t != NULL)`, and use it at all 11 call sites instead of the
  repeated two-line pattern.

## Files touched
- `tests/test_rbtree.c` — new rotation-coverage tests + all cleanup items.
- `tests/test_rbtree_whitebox.c` — new file, white-box `rb_validate`
  negative tests.
- `Makefile` — new `WBSRC`/`WBBIN` build rule (same shape as `$(FUZZBIN)`),
  added to `all`, `test`, and `memcheck` targets.
- No changes to `src/rbtree.c` or `include/rbtree.h`.

## Commits (small slices, per CLAUDE.md)
1. `M1: add insert tests for LL/LR/RL rotation coverage` — black-box,
   `tests/test_rbtree.c` only.
2. `M1: add white-box negative tests for rb_validate` — new file +
   Makefile.
3. `M1: test cleanup — assert side effects, dedupe fixtures, bounds check`
   — remaining cleanup items in `tests/test_rbtree.c`.

Each commit only happens after `make test`, `make asan`, and `make
memcheck` all pass (clean `make clean` before `memcheck` to avoid the
stale-ASan-binary issue hit earlier this session).

## Verification
`module load gcc/15.2.0`, then `make test`, `make asan`, `make clean &&
make memcheck` after each of the 3 slices, showing real output each time,
matching the existing pattern from this session.

# Address /code-review findings on tests/

## Context
`/code-review tests/` ran against the M1 commits just made (rb_find, rb_insert
tests, rb_validate) and returned 6 confirmed findings. The user asked to fix
all of them. Two are a real coverage gap in the algorithm's test surface,
one needs new test infrastructure, and three are cleanup/robustness nits:

1. **No test ever drives `insert_fixup`'s LL-rotation or either zigzag
   (LR/RL) double-rotation branch** — every existing insert sequence only
   hits the "uncle red" recolor case or a straight RR rotation. A bug in
   `src/rbtree.c:106-133` would pass the whole suite silently.
2. **`rb_validate` is never tested against a genuinely invalid tree** — it's
   only ever run on trees `insert_fixup` already made correct, so a broken
   validator (e.g. always returning 0) would go undetected.
3. `collect_key` in `tests/test_rbtree.c` writes into `order_ctx_t.keys[64]`
   with no bounds check.
4. `assert(rb_insert(...) == 0)` performs the mutating call *inside* the
   assert, so the call vanishes under `-DNDEBUG`.
5. The `{"mango","kiwi","pear","fig","lime","apricot"}` fixture is
   copy-pasted across two tests.
6. All 11 test functions repeat the same `rb_create` + `assert(!=NULL)`
   boilerplate.

Findings 1 and 2 need different fixes. (1) is testable with the *existing*
public API — specific 3-key insertion orders force each rotation branch, and
`rb_validate` (already proven correct by the M1 work) is the black-box
oracle that would catch a broken rotation. (2) is not testable through the
public API at all: `rb_insert`'s fixup always leaves a correct tree, and

produce an invalid tree through `include/rbtree.h`'s frozen surface. Testing
`rb_validate`'s negative cases requires white-box access to the internal
`rb_node_t`/`rbtree_t` layout, which only exists in `src/rbtree.c`.

Add a new test translation unit, `tests/test_rbtree_whitebox.c`, that does
`#include "../src/rbtree.c"` instead of `#include "rbtree.h"` — a standard
C "unity build" pattern that pulls in `rb_node_t`, `rbtree_t`, `RB_RED`/

git add tests/test_rbtree_whitebox.c Makefile && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
M1: add white-box negative tests for rb_validate

rb_insert's fixup always leaves a correct tree and rb_delete isn't
implemented yet, so no invalid tree is reachable through the public
API -- rb_validate's negative cases were previously untested, meaning
a silently-broken validator would pass the whole suite.

Adds tests/test_rbtree_whitebox.c, which #includes src/rbtree.c
directly to get at rb_node_t/rbtree_t internals without touching the
frozen include/rbtree.h, and hand-builds trees that each isolate one
of the 5 rb_validate checks (red root, red-red violation, black-height
mismatch, out-of-order keys, size mismatch), plus a valid hand-built
tree as a control. New WBBIN Makefile target compiles it standalone
(not linked against src/rbtree.c again, since it's pulled in via
#include) and wires it into test/asan/memcheck.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_012hpoRLy7NuNsDdwJqZ4Btt
EOF
)"
